name: Comfort Systems USA

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Comfort Systems USA logo.svg)

description: Comfort Systems USA is a US mechanical and electrical contractor: it designs, installs and services heating, cooling, plumbing, piping, controls, fire protection and electrical systems, plus off-site prefabrication (modular) work. About 63% of FY2025 revenue was new construction and 23% work in existing buildings; 45% of revenue came from technology-sector customers (up from 33% in 2024 and 21% in 2023), mainly data-center builders, ahead of manufacturing (22%) and healthcare (9%). Projects are priced up front and revenue is recognised as cost is incurred (cost-to-cost method), so margin depends on estimating and execution; backlog of signed project work was $14.06 billion at June 30, 2026, up 73% in a year.

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Industrials' and Sub-Industry 'Construction & Engineering' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30; added Dec 22, 2025). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry. SEC SIC code 1731 (Electrical Work) per EDGAR. The box hides that 45% of FY2025 revenue came from technology-sector customers (data centers and similar).

hq.note: 9753 Katy Freeway, Suite 700, Houston, TX 77024 (EDGAR business address)

employees.note: About 22,700 employees vs about 18,300 a year earlier; collective bargaining covers 9 employees (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Mechanical segment
businessLines.how: Building owners and general contractors (increasingly data-center developers) sign priced projects for design and installation; revenue is recognised as costs are incurred, and profit is the margin over labour, materials and subcontractors; service work and short jobs billed as performed do not go through backlog.
businessLines.description: HVAC, plumbing, piping and controls, plus off-site construction (modular and prefabrication), monitoring and fire protection.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating income before corporate costs

businessLines.name: Electrical segment
businessLines.how: Same priced-project model as mechanical, for electrical installations (with a large data-center share, the Texas electrical operation added about $1.0B of backlog in Q2 2026); profit is the margin over labour and materials.
businessLines.description: Installation and servicing of electrical systems.

brands.name: Acquired operating companies: Right Way, Century, Summit, J&S (mechanical, FY2025); Feyen Zylstra, Meisner (electrical, FY2025); Hunt (included in Q2 2026 backlog)
brands.share: Acquisitions added $169.3M to mechanical FY2025 revenue and $66.8M to electrical; Hunt added $217.4M of backlog in Q2 2026
